target_customer: Patients with gastrointestinal disease such as ulcerative colitis, reached through pharma partners and clinicians
problem: Systemic drugs for gut disorders cause side effects and reach the diseased gut poorly. Intact develops thermosensitive gels and micelle formulations for local delivery in the digestive tract.
business_model: Biopharma platform: develop and license or partner local drug delivery products
product_category: Local drug delivery for GI disease

founders.name: Ravi Pamnani
founders.background_notes: YC bio says only that he is passionate about the intersection of health and technology.

founders.name: Sidhartha Sinha
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no bio. Spelled Sidharta Sinha, MD in one Rosenman Institute listing seen in search results.

technical_complexity.rationale: Drug delivery materials and formulations need preclinical and clinical development with regulatory approval, which is hard for a four person team.

defensibility.rationale: Licensed Stanford-origin thermogel platform and clinical data can be protected by patents and approvals, but academic groups publish similar thermosensitive gels.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action was found in the sources.

market_need_then: Ulcerative colitis and other GI disorders have large patient populations and side effects from systemic drugs. A 2015 Stanford study showed a thermosensitive gel improved colitis in mice, and a small Phase 1 study followed.

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence found. Site lists logos of Encube Ethicals, Y Combinator, Stanford, BrightStone, UCSF Rosenman Institute and Mehta Ventures.

brand_strength.rationale: Search results were swamped by similarly named companies such as Intract Pharma and Interact Therapeutics, and no press about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Intact is active and small. It has run a Phase 1 study of a thermal gel for ulcerative colitis and now describes itself as clinical-stage. Funding found is small and grant based, and a stated goal of a $20M Series A is undated and unconfirmed. It is a long-cycle biotech that has not yet reached the milestone for a large round.
notes: Competitor list is empty: search found only academic papers on thermosensitive gels, no dated company rivals near 2019. Aggregators conflict: CB Insights lists about $370K over 3 rounds including an NSF grant of $220K in August 2020, VCBacked lists a November 2021 Series A with no amount. These are single aggregator claims and unverified, so they are not recorded as rounds. The $20M Series A target comes from an undated BIO conference listing. Founder employers and education were not found in an opened source. The outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition.
